newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul shares post selective gains.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul shares post selective gains.

text.p: Istanbul's stock market index extended morning gains on selective afternoon purchases on Wednesday following a four-day holiday, brokers said.

But the majority of the shares, 122 out of 227 traded, fell, 81 rose and 24 were unchanged. The IMKB-100 closed at 83,692.58, up 1,271.6 points, or 1.54 percent from Friday, compared to a 1.24 percent gain in the morning.
The bourse was closed on Monday and Tuesday due to Republic day.
Trade volume surged to 20.65 trillion lira from Friday's 12.84 trillion.

Brokers said largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, a bluechip, was among the top earners with a 14.3 percent jump from Friday to 12,000 lira and was a major factor behind the index's rise due to its high market capitalisation.

Eregli was the third most heavily traded stock after utility Aktas Elektrik which firmed 5,000 lira to 88,000 and Cukurova Elektrik which rose 8,000 lira to 78,000. Kepez Elektrik, up 2,000 lira to 88,000 was the fourth most active issue.
Together, the four made up 41.1 percent of the total turnover.
"The market became highly selective with players mostly switching shares depending on companies' nine-month profits," said Resat Kutucular from Toros securities.
Companies released their nine-month financial results over the weekend. Banks have until November 8 to report.

"Technically, the index is at a critical level from where it can move either way. Sentiment looks good, but there is no substantial reason to back a rally. So if the index slips below 81,000, it may fall towards 75,000," Kutucular said.
Some brokers expect range-bound trade between 81,000 and 84,000 unless fresh cash inflow increases to push the market to new highs.
The index had surged 29.3 percent from September 13 to last Wednesday's all-time high close of 83,772.33, the tenth record in the medium-term uptrend which began with the breaching of 65,000 level.
The 85-share industrial index gained 1.72 percent to 88,562.19 and the 15-share financial index rose 1.15 percent to 80,723.57.
